explicit_validation.explanation: Paper explicitly compares LLM-based evaluations against human assessments across three tasks (Solution Checker, Domain Compliance, Response Quality) using accuracy metrics to measure alignment

prompts.notes: Full prompt texts provided in Appendix H (H.1, H.2, H.3) and Appendix J (J.6) with in-context examples and detailed instructions

inter_annotator_agreement.interpretation: demonstrating the reliability of our annotations across all domains

guidelines.notes: Annotators were provided with the exact same instructions as the LLM evaluation prompts (H.2, H.3, J) ensuring consistency between human and LLM evaluations

sample_size.notes: Validation performed on a sample set for each task, with 10% of data used for dual annotations to measure inter-annotator agreement

correlation_interpretation.threshold_used: High accuracy numbers (94-97%) considered strong alignment

validation_results.summary_finding: LLM-based evaluations show strong alignment with human judgments across all three tasks (94-97% accuracy), supporting the potential for fully automating the evaluation process without compromising reliability.

criteria_mapping.notes: Human evaluation was conducted specifically to validate the LLM evaluations on the shared criteria, while evaluation metrics specific to Retrieval Performance and Turn Optimization were only assessed by LLM
